> I can't reproduce it. The following code works as expected:

I also was unable to replicate the issue with a simple example.  Per my post, I tried the same setup you did as well as using a similar setup with two files with `class_name`.

Did you try the "Steps to Reproduce"?

> You should specify Variant on the parent method (or omit the return type)...

This is what I did.  I changed the signature in `GutTest` to `func should_skip_script() -> Variant:`.  As I stated this might work, but makes the return type required.  In the examples I gave, if the parent's method has an explicit return type then any sub classes that contain paths that do not return a value will cause errors.

> Therefore, it can only be considered a bug if GDScript in some cases implicitly infers the return type of a non-overridden method using return statements, despite the absence of an explicit return type in the function header.

I believe this is what is happening.  In this case GDScript is inferring that the return type of the base class method is `bool` even though no return type is explicitly declared (`GutTest` extends `Node`).  It is then giving a parser error in a subclass that overrides that method because it attempts to return a string.

If you follow the steps to reproduce and attempt to run tests you will get the parser error that is in the screenshot.  You can see from the screenshot that the script is extending `GutTest`.  Here is the signature from `GutTest` which extends `Node` (yes I know it says "Virtual" and the method is not virtual, this was written before actual virtual methods existed.):
```
## Virtual Method.  This is run after the script has been prepped for execution, but before `before_all` is executed.  If you implement this method and return `true` or a `String` (the string is displayed in the log) then GUT will stop executing the script and mark it as risky.  You might want to do this because:
## - You are porting tests from 3.x to 4.x and you don't want to comment everything out.[br]
## - Skipping tests that should not be run when in `headless` mode such as input testing that does not work in headless.[br]
## [codeblock]
##    func should_skip_script():
##        if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless":
##            return "Skip Input tests when running headless"
## [/codeblock]
## - If you have tests that would normally cause the debugger to break on an error, you can skip the script if the debugger is enabled so that the run is not interrupted.[br]
## [codeblock]
##    func should_skip_script():
##        return EngineDebugger.is_active()
## [/codeblock]
func should_skip_script():
	return false
```
https://github.com/bitwes/Gut/blob/372cddcfeef468fed87bb4f9038f31ab4d604b5f/addons/gut/test.gd#L413

Yes, I noticed this later and therefore added the "needs testing" label. I clarified this just in case, to avoid any possible misunderstanding. Your project is quite large, and contributors are more comfortable analyzing MRP. I have a couple of guesses as to what might be causing the bug, but without being able to reproduce the problem, I'm not sure I fully understand it and won't be able to verify that a potential fix completely addresses the issue.

If it's not too much trouble, please try making a copy of your project and iteratively removing parts that seem unrelated to the bug. If at some point the bug disappears, take a step back. Continue until the project is small enough for analysis but still reproduces the bug. I or another contributor could try to do this ourselves without knowing your project. But you, as the author, probably have a better chance of extracting the MRP faster (since you know which parts of the project depend on each other and which don't).

Ok. Since I couldn't reproduce easily, I was hoping this would sound familiar to someone who could narrow it down easier from the Godot side. I see in that issue you linked that the probable cause is only a single line of code, which doesn't help much in finding the root cause. I have made a few attempts at simplifying the issue but haven't had much luck. The best I have so far is to install the GUT plugin into a new project and create this: `res://extends_gut_test.gd` ``` extends GutTest func should_skip_script(): return "hello world" ``` This will cause the error in the editor: The odd thing, is that if I create a scene with the following script, it runs fine and prints "hello world" ``` extends Node2D var ExtendsGutTest = load('res://extends_gut_test.gd') func _ready(): var inst = ExtendsGutTest.new() print(inst.should_skip_script()) ``` I'll continue to try and narrow things down. I've attached the project with GUT which includes the script and scene mentioned above. [ExampleWithGut.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25777906/ExampleWithGut.zip)

I was able to narrow down the issue, needs two classes in separated scripts and the class that will be inherited needs to have an inner class. The bug comes when you create a new instance of the inner class inside the inherited class: ``` main_class.gd class_name MainClass class MainClassInner: # Ironically calling inside the proper class doesn't trigget the bug var n = MainClassInner.new() # This causes the bug var a = MainClassInner.new() func why_is_asking_for_other_type(): # This causes the bug MainClassInner.new() return 1 # This causes the bug MainClassInner.new() # This causes the bug var b = MainClassInner.new() func other_func(): # This causes the bug MainClassInner.new() ``` ``` # second_class.gd extends MainClass func why_is_asking_for_other_type(): return "" # Error at (4, 5): Cannot return value of type "String" because the function return type is "int". ```

I'll bisect this.
Reverting PR #115763 fixes the error. Pinging @dalexeev to confirm if this is a valid bug before ping the PR author
Reverting PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115763 also fixes the "Double" errors I was seeing.  With this change reverted, all of the GUT tests pass.
